ranked_evidence.title: Norovirus know-how: Tips to manage symptoms and contain the spread | Prevention | Public Health | UT Southwestern Medical Center
ranked_evidence.snippet: # Norovirus know-how: Tips to manage symptoms and contain the spread. There is no effective treatment for norovirus, which is highly contagious. Norovirus is a gastrointestinal virus that is as common as it is cunning. Infected people develop sudden, explosive vomiting and diarrhea that gets sprayed through the air when expelled by the body or when the toilet is flushed. And hundreds of cruise ship passengers are infected each year in a myriad of ways, from touching tainted buffet utensils to getting up close and personal in the conga line. But those who are immunocompromised, such as after an organ transplant, are at risk of developing chronic vomiting and diarrhea – sometimes lasting several years since there isn’t an effective antiviral treatment and/or vaccine to prevent norovirus infection. The best way to reduce your risk is to be able to recognize norovirus symptoms and follow best practices to contain the spread.

ranked_evidence.title: Norovirus: Symptoms, Causes & Treatment
ranked_evidence.snippet: Norovirus is a common and very contagious virus. Your symptoms may be similar to the stomach flu, but they have a different cause. Norovirus is a group of viruses that causes severe vomiting and diarrhea. It’s a very common illness and it’s very contagious. #### What is the difference between norovirus and the stomach flu? It’s in the *Caliciviridae* family of viruses that cause inflammation of your stomach and intestines (gastroenteritis). ### What are the symptoms of norovirus? #### Are norovirus symptoms the same in children and adults? Symptoms of norovirus are usually the same in both children and adults. A virus in the *Caliciviridae* family causes norovirus. Norovirus is the biggest cause of illness from contaminated food in the U.S. The virus typically spreads when someone who has the virus touches food before serving it to someone else. Norovirus can make it difficult for you to eat or drink because the inflammation in your intestines and stomach causes you to vomit or have diarrhea.
